Our leading performers in the County Championships were Ranjit Bhatia, 1st Oxfordshire; Charlie Dabbs 11th Suurey; Pat Newell 17th Middlesex; and David Jones 17th Hampshire.
A field of 28 lined up for the start and within half a mile Dabbs, Walker, Newell and David Jones were running together, 35 yards clear of the field.

After 2½ miles Charlie was 5th, followed by Ken Miller 28th, David Jones 46th, Ranjit Bhatia 53rd, John Moore 60th, Clive Shippen 61st, and Ken Venton 82nd, with the others at regularly spaced intervals within the first half of the field.

David Jones, Clive Shippen, and Eric Gebbett were always together near the hundred mark and it was the last mile which enabled David to gain the few extra places for 97th, ahead of Clive at 107th and Eric, dropping slightly to 122.
166 · D. F. Jones · Belgrave

Brian Hallowell produced an encouraging performance in taking us back into the lead once more and David Jones ran consistently in improving the margin to 20 secs; leaving Newell and Dabbs to do no more than underline our superiority.

David Jones was our runner on Stage 7. Twelve months ago no one would have even considered David as a Brighton prospect but hard work and determined effort have produced a most stylish and relaxed performer who has shown most consistent running throughout the winter.

David Jones, who had finished third in our championship the previous week to surprise us all, again ran well. The next major event was the Southern at Parliament Hill but our running was nothing to raise any enthusiasm over although we did secure the 'twelve' cup for Surrey clubs.

In the 3,000 metres team event our only starter was David Jones who had travelled all the way from Chichester. He was well up with the leaders until 2 laps to go when he faded rather badly, finishing in an equivalent 2 mile time of 9-34.0.
